competitive_landscape: The bay is served today by an intense incumbent fast-ferry network — Caremar, SNAV, Alilauro and NLG — running diesel hydrofoils year-round. That density is exactly the demand proof: islands already organise their lives around the boat. But the fleet is noisy, fuel-burning, wake-heavy and timetable-bound, and Capri's peak-day caps and queues expose the gap for a quiet, guaranteed-seat, zero-emission tier. There is no on-demand or foiling-clean option in the bay today.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Pioneer II owns the entire Bay of Naples necklace — Beverello↔Procida (~13 nm), Naples↔Ischia (~18 nm), Naples↔Capri (~17 nm), Capri↔Sorrento (~12 nm), Capri↔Amalfi (~16 nm). Every core leg sits inside the 70 nm all-electric envelope with margin for many daily rotations; the sheltered gulf and wake-light foiling suit dense port traffic and resident-island ports.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Quanta-LR (commercial H2 2026+, hybrid, no charging-infra dependency) extends the bay outward on long open-water legs — toward the Pontine Islands (Ponza ~33 nm Pioneer-range but exposed) and the longer seasonal reach to the Aeolian archipelago (~120 nm) — without depending on island charging.

regulatory_note: Italian flag / EU regime under the Capitaneria di Porto (Italian Coast Guard). The Gulf of Naples falls within the Mediterranean SOx Emission Control Area (effective 2025) and EU FuelEU Maritime pressure on diesel passenger craft, creating a clean-fleet tailwind. The Punta Campanella Marine Protected Area on the Sorrento peninsula favours low-wake, zero-emission vessels; Capri's day-visitor cap pushes the market toward higher-value, lower-volume premium marine mobility.
seasonality: Year-round demand on the resident-island corridors (Ischia/Procida), with an intense April–October tourism surge peaking June–September. The protected gulf is sheltered most of the year; winter NW winds bring occasional chop on the outer Capri leg — conditions where foiling's smoother, more reliable ride becomes the premium.

summary: The Bay of Naples is where Europe already commutes and holidays by fast boat: Caremar, SNAV, Alilauro and NLG run an intense year-round aliscafo (hydrofoil) network from Naples-Beverello out to Procida, Ischia, Capri, Sorrento and Pozzuoli. The gulf is sheltered, the legs are short (all well under 20 nm), and the islands of Ischia and Procida depend on the sea every day of the year for residents, school, work and supplies — then surge with summer tourism (Procida was Italian Capital of Culture 2022). It is a rare triple market in one bay: an island public-transport lifeline, an on-demand ridehail layer, and a Capri luxury-transfer tier — all on diesel hydrofoils today, none of it quiet, clean or on-demand.
tagline: The densest hydrofoil market in the Western Mediterranean — a protected gulf where islands already live by the boat.
